Networking: VPC peering, private endpoints, ingress patterns
Security: KMS/HSM integration, audit logs, SSO for console
Performance: quantization choices, benchmarking and cost tradeoffs
Next steps: runbook, sample chart, POC planning
transcript:
[00:00] Samira Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um this is Samira from Redwood, AE on the account. We'll do quick intros, then Ethan will take the technical piece.  
[00:18] Lena Ortiz: Hi all, Lena here, head of platform at Verdant Sky. Appreciate you coordinating. We want to get a clear path to listing on the cloud marketplace and ensure our customers can deploy to VPCs and on-prem.
[00:32] Ethan Cole: Hi, Ethan, Redwood SE. Quick agenda: packaging options (helm vs operator), network patterns for private listing, KMS and audit flow, and quantization/benchmark guidance. We'll leave time for Q&A.
[00:48] Raj Mehra: Quick thing — our security team insists on customer-managed keys and auditability. Also we have a couple of regulated workloads so data never leaves their VPC unless explicitly routed.
[01:02] Ethan Cole: OK, that's doable; Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and we have an onprem package. For marketplace marketplace listing we typically provide a marketplace connector that can run as a helm chart inside the customer's cluster or as a dedicated managed node set.
[01:25] Marta Lopez: When you say connector, is that a sidecar or a standalone service? We're worried about network egress and NAT.
[01:35] Ethan Cole: Good question — it's a standalone deployment (Deployment + Service) that establishes a private, TLS-mutual channel to the Redwood control plane for billing/metrics only. Data plane can stay in VPC depending on the pattern. There are two main patterns: 1) Bring-your-own nodes where inference runs locally, 2) Remote-hosted inference with a private endpoint.
[02:02] Darren Chu: And for the marketplace UX, customers expect a one-click deploy to their cluster. Does Redwood provide that?
[02:10] Samira Patel: We can provide a marketplace listing artifact that triggers a helm install with presets for required RBAC and KMS policies. We'll need Verdant Sky to confirm the default namespace and any custom resources.
[02:26] Raj Mehra: Our infra uses strict Pod Security Policies and we also require encrypted ephemeral storage. Are there any privileged permissions in the helm chart?
[02:37] Ethan Cole: No privileged containers. We do need permissions for creating ConfigMaps, ServiceAccounts, Roles for metrics and optionally a CSI for KMS-based secrets sync. We can document a minimal RBAC footprint.
[02:53] Lena Ortiz: What about HSM integration? We use an HSM-backed KMS for some PII workloads.
[03:01] Ethan Cole: Redwood supports external KMS via standard APIs; HSM is fine as long as it presents the compatible KMS interface. We'll need to test the key rotation logic in your environment; that's part of the POC.
[03:18] Samira Patel: On the listing side, marketplace vendors typically need a listing tile, icon, description, and a deployment artifact. We'll share our listing checklist after this call.
[03:30] Marta Lopez: Regarding quantization — we run smaller GPUs for cost reasons; do you recommend INT8 or FP16 for our models?
[03:38] Ethan Cole: It depends on model family. For most transformer-based open models, int8 via dynamic quantization gives great cost savings with small quality delta. But if you have custom LLMs with some layer norms that are sensitive, FP16 might be safer. We'll run a quantization sweep during POC.
[03:58] Raj Mehra: Can you also show us expected latency numbers for both hosted and dedicated? We need to include this in our internal TCO.
[04:06] Ethan Cole: Sure — typical numbers: hosted (multi-tenant) 80–250ms token latency for small models with streaming, dedicated can push tail latency below 50ms depending on GPU and sequence length. We'll provide an annotated benchmark worksheet.
[04:25] Darren Chu: How do you handle fallbacks? If dedicated is full, can traffic route to a compatible variant to avoid outages?
[04:33] Ethan Cole: Yes, smart routing can failover to a compatible model variant or to another region. We surface these as policies in the deployment manifest.
[04:45] Lena Ortiz: Audit logs — we need per-request provenance for compliance. Does Redwood expose request-level logs and token-level costs?
[04:55] Samira Patel: Redwood Console has request-level tracing, token breakdowns, and configurable retention. For Private installs we can forward logs to your SIEM or S3.
[05:06] Marta Lopez: A bit about packaging — our ops team prefers a single helm chart that can toggle between onprem and remote modes with values.yaml. Is that pattern supported?
[05:16] Ethan Cole: Absolutely. We usually ship a values schema with a mode field: local|hybrid|remote. We'll include examples.
[05:24] Raj Mehra: Any preflight checks for networking? It'd be great if the helm chart runs a quick connectivity test to endpoints and KMS reachability.
[05:33] Ethan Cole: Good suggestion — we can add a post-install Job that verifies endpoints, certs, and KMS handshake. We'll push a sample script.
[05:46] Lena Ortiz: For billing when listed in marketplace, does usage flow through their marketplace billing or direct Redwood billing?
[05:55] Samira Patel: We support marketplace metering integrations; depending on the marketplace you can choose vendor-billed or partner-billed. We'll prepare options and examples — includes per-token metering or per-invocation.
[06:07] Marta Lopez: On the POC scope, what should we plan to validate in week one vs week two?
[06:12] Ethan Cole: Week one: install helm chart in your dev cluster, validate RBAC/KMS connectivity, run small benchmark. Week two: quantization sweep, run 1,000 conformance prompts, and integrate audit logs to your SIEM.
[06:26] Darren Chu: Security review — our legal wants SOC2 evidence and a pen-test report. Do you have templated artifacts?
[06:34] Samira Patel: Yes, we'll share SOC 2 summary, an SOC letter, and a pen-test summary. For Marketplace listing you often attach those to the vendor profile.
[06:45] Raj Mehra: On the technical deep dive, can Ethan walk through the network diagram?
[06:50] Ethan Cole: Sure — I'll share my screen after the call notes; I'll produce a diagram that shows control plane only egress, optional private link/endpoint, and local inference with KV cache remaining in the customer's VPC.
[07:04] Lena Ortiz: Regarding KV cache, we need guarantees around cache eviction and customer data not being stored beyond session.
[07:12] Ethan Cole: KV cache is per-request ephemeral; we don't persist customer data in long-term storage unless configured for caching across sessions. We'll annotate the behavior in the runbook.
[07:25] Marta Lopez: Any known issues with older Kubernetes versions? We run 1.21 clusters in some pockets.
[07:33] Ethan Cole: Minimum supported is 1.22 for the operator, but helm-based deploys can run on 1.21 with degraded metrics if API versions are older. We'll include compatibility matrix.
[07:45] Samira Patel: Ok, let's surface the most important blockers for you. Lena?
[07:51] Lena Ortiz: 1) KMS/HSM validation; 2) RBAC and PSP confirmation; 3) Marketplace billing model decision. If those three are OK we can go to POC.
[08:03] Samira Patel: Great — we'll prioritize KMS runbook and the helm chart skeleton. Ethan will own the runbook.
[08:10] Ethan Cole: I'll also draft the post-install checks and sample values.yaml.
[08:16] Raj Mehra: For benchmarking, we'll provide a traffic profile and expected concurrency numbers — Marta will collect that and share.
[08:24] Marta Lopez: Yes, I'll send the VM/instance types and average concurrency by 7/14.
[08:30] Darren Chu: Anything else on compliance?
[08:32] Samira Patel: We'll package SOC2 artifacts plus the security questionnaire template.
[08:38] Lena Ortiz: Timeline check — can we aim to have the marketplace listing readiness artifacts in two weeks?
[08:44] Samira Patel: Yes, Redwood can get the initial checklist and helm skeleton to you by 2026-07-13.
[08:51] Ethan Cole: And POC planning session scheduled for 2026-07-21 — Samira will send calendar invite after this call.
[09:00] Samira Patel: Recap: Redwood to share listing checklist, sample helm chart, and KMS runbook. Verdant Sky to share cluster sizing, compliance doc, and traffic profile. We'll do a 2-hour POC planning on 7/21. Any other blockers?
[09:16] Raj Mehra: No, that sounds good. One small ask — include a short FAQ for our sales ops for marketplace tile wording.
[09:24] Samira Patel: Will do, short FAQ included in the package.
[09:28] Lena Ortiz: Thanks everyone.
[09:30] Samira Patel: Thanks all, we'll follow up with links. Meeting adjourned.
